opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jesus Cooke (employee ID E029) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E029.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Employee is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write (admin only if role owns the system; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code). Requested level equals the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows employee is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read without advanced training (write requires advanced). Requested write exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: The two team notes conflict on employment type: HR lists full_time (max write for Source Code), while Security lists contractor with basic security training (max read, since write requires advanced training). Given the conflicting evidence, I apply the more restrictive Access policy to avoid over-granting. As a contractor with basic training, the maximum allowed level is read, and the requested write exceeds that, so the granted level is read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Jesus Cooke (E029), requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes:
1. HR note: role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Full-time up to write, admin only if role owns system. Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code. Requested level equals maximum, so recommend write.

2. Security note: role Payroll Specialist (not looked up), employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Contractors max is read without advanced training. Requested write exceeds maximum, so recommend read.

Conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. The employee facts differ. HR looked up employment type in own database; Security looked up employment type in own database. Hmm.

How to decide? The security note says "Security DB shows employee is a contractor with basic security training." The HR note says "full_time" looked up in own database. Both claim to look up.

We have conflicting facts. Which to trust? The security team's database might be more authoritative for employment type? Actually, HR usually owns employment type. But the security note explicitly says looked up in own database.

The access policy: contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training → max read. Requested write → grant read.

Full-time: up to write. Requested write → grant write.

The conflict matters. Since the two notes conflict, I need to decide. Typically the approver must make a decision based on available info. The HR note says full-time with write recommendation. The security note says contractor with basic training and read recommendation.

Which is more reliable? The security agent says "looked up in own database" for employment type; HR also "looked up in own database." Hmm.

We have two database sources disagreeing. Without more info, perhaps we should take the more restrictive level? The policy is about max access. If uncertain, grant the safer (lower) level. Applying security's data: contractor, basic training → read. That seems safer.

Also, consider the security note says role was "not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1" - the role is from HR. Employment type from security DB is contractor. HR says full-time.

Given the conflict, the conservative approach is to grant the lower maximum. Also note the access policy says contractor with basic training max read. Grant read.

I'll submit read.
